title: RYU OKA: A Silk Route Table At 11,562 Feet
author: The Grand Dragon Ladakh
excerpt: RYU OKA is a Pan-Asian restaurant at The Grand Dragon Ladakh, inspired by the historic Silk Route, bringing together flavors from Japan, Korea, Thailand, China, and Bali at 11,562 feet altitude in Leh.
content: Long before it was a destination for travellers, Ladakh was a crossroads — a high, cold junction where caravans carrying silk, tea, and spice moved between India, Tibet, and Central Asia. RYU OKA, The Grand Dragon Ladakh's new Pan-Asian restaurant, is built around that history rather than around it.

sections.title: The Idea Behind RYU OKA
sections.content: RYU OKA was developed specifically around the cultural and culinary exchanges of the historic Silk Route — not as a loose theme, but as an actual curatorial principle for the menu.

sections.title: How the Meal Begins
sections.content: Before the menu proper arrives, guests at RYU OKA are served a small, specific ritual: a shot of roasted barley water, warm and earthy, more grounding than a conventional welcome drink.

sections.title: What's Actually on the Table
sections.content: The kitchen at RYU OKA works local ingredients into a genuinely Pan-Asian repertoire — apricot, barley, sea buckthorn, and buckwheat appear across selected dishes.
dishes: Mongol Wrapped Tofu with collard greens

sections.title: The Bar: Built for Altitude
sections.content: RYU OKA's drinks programme takes Ladakh's elevation seriously rather than treating it as an afterthought.

sections.title: The Room Itself
sections.content: RYU OKA occupies a lobby-level space decorated with colourful, traditional Ladakhi frescos with a patio offering views of the Stok Kangri mountain range.

faqs.question: What kind of restaurant is RYU OKA?
faqs.answer: RYU OKA is a Pan-Asian restaurant at The Grand Dragon Ladakh, inspired by the historic Silk Route, bringing together the flavours of Japan, Korea, Thailand, China, and Bali.

faqs.question: What are the signature dishes at RYU OKA?
faqs.answer: Mongol Wrapped Tofu with collard greens, the RYU OKA Clay Pot, and Truffle Fried Rice, alongside other dishes that incorporate local Ladakhi ingredients such as apricot, sea buckthorn, and buckwheat.

faqs.question: Does RYU OKA serve alcohol-free options?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Sea Buckthorn Spritz is available as both a cocktail and an alcohol-free mocktail, and traditional non-alcoholic options like Hot Butter Tea and Kahwa are also on the menu.

faqs.question: Where is RYU OKA located within The Grand Dragon Ladakh?
faqs.answer: On the lobby level, in a room decorated with traditional Ladakhi frescos, with a patio offering views of the Stok Kangri mountain range.

faqs.question: Is The Grand Dragon Ladakh a five-star hotel?
faqs.answer: Yes, it is one of Leh's established luxury hotels, located at P. Namgyal Road, Sheynam, in the heart of the city.

faqs.question: Why does RYU OKA serve a barley water shot before the meal?
faqs.answer: Barley has been a staple crop in Ladakh for centuries, traditionally roasted and used in local food and drink. Opening the meal with a roasted barley water shot ties the Pan-Asian menu back to the region's own food culture.

contact.location: P. Namgyal Road, Sheynam, Leh, Ladakh — 194101
